items.title: VIDEO: Millions watch as influencer Jordan The Stallion visits Mississauga food plaza
items.summary: One of Mississauga’s most talked-about food destinations has caught the attention of one of social media’s biggest stars. Jordan Howlett, better known as Jordan “The Stallion,” recently stopped at Ridgeway Plaza, where he sampled desserts at two local businesses and brought the popular food hub to the attention of his enormous online following. Howlett visited Nora Cakes & Sweets, trying its cookie dough and ice cream, before heading to The Dough Diaries, where he sampled the shop’s Original Pudding Cake. For the two local dessert businesses, having Howlett walk through the door is potentially significant exposure. The American content creator has built a massive following on TikTok and Instagram, with his combined audience now numbering in the tens of millions. He became widely known for his humorous food commentary and his “Fast Food Secrets Club,” in which he shares tips, observations and behind-the-scenes information about fast-food favourites. His videos are also recognizable for his trademark bathroom-mirror introductions, often beginning with his now-famous “Come here” catchphrase. That audience includes a large number of younger viewers and food enthusiasts, making a stop at a local restaurant or dessert shop considerably more than just a celebrity visit. And Howlett chose an interesting place to make his Mississauga food stop.

items.title: Topps turns Josh Naylor into the “Mississauga Masher" on rare baseball card
items.summary: If you happen to open a pack of baseball cards this year and come across one that says “Mississauga Masher” across the front, you might wonder what exactly you’re looking at. For baseball fans in Mississauga, however, the answer is pretty easy. ” And for a city that doesn’t exactly have a long history of appearing on the front of major-league baseball cards, it’s a pretty big deal. The card is one of just 10 Nickname Variations included in the 2026 Topps Heritage set, which pays tribute to the classic 1977 Topps design. Other players receiving the nickname treatment include Bobby Witt Jr. (“Bobby Baseball”), Kyle Schwarber (“Schwarbs”), Cal Raleigh (“Big Dumper”) and Roman Anthony (“Roman Empire”). But only one of them has his hometown featured quite so prominently. Naylor’s card is No. 129 in the set and shows the Seattle Mariners first baseman with “Mississauga Masher” where collectors would normally expect to see his name. The variation is a short print, meaning collectors are considerably less likely to find it than the standard Naylor card. For Mississauga, there is an added bit of novelty.

items.title: $100K cocaine bust near Niagara Falls, Ontario leads to charges for Mississauga man
items.summary: A Mississauga man faces charges following an investigation by police into the alleged selling of cocaine near Niagara Falls. Two search warrants executed on Tuesday in Welland and Thorold led to the recovery by police of more than $100,000 in suspected cocaine and nearly $50,000 in cash. The raids, carried out by street crime unit officers with Niagara Regional Police, also resulted in the arrests of a Mississauga man and a woman from Welland, police said. The investigation began in July when Niagara detectives started looking into the suspected sale of cocaine by a man in St. Catharines, located just outside Niagara Falls. The execution of the pair of search warrants on Tuesday resulted in the recovery by police of: Ismail Ahmed, 30, of Mississauga, is charged with: The accused remains in custody and is scheduled to appear for a bail hearing Wednesday in St. Catharines court. Chantal Fournier, 35, of Welland, is charged with possession of proceeds of property obtained by crime over $5,000. She was released with a future court date that’s yet to be set, police said.

items.title: No fireworks unless you have a permit over Labour Day weekend in Mississauga
items.summary: Backyard fireworks displays over the Labour Day long weekend in Mississauga are not permitted unless residents first get the go-ahead from the city. Celebrating with fireworks anywhere in the city on any day throughout the upcoming weekend, including the holiday Monday, requires a permit, according to the City of Mississauga. In Mississauga, fireworks displays are only allowed at home without a permit on Victoria Day, Canada Day, Diwali, Lunar New Year and New Year’s Eve. In place of fireworks, city officials have suggested in past years that people celebrate with glow sticks, noisemakers or sparklers. As usual on holiday weekends, Mississauga bylaw enforcement officers will be out in full force to ensure fireworks aren’t being sold or used illegally. Those who want to submit complaints about illegal use of fireworks, and residents seeking general information, can visit the city’s website and search “fireworks” or call the city’s information/reporting line at 311. Dozens of complaints this past Canada Day According to the city, Mississauga residents registered 58 fireworks use complaints with the city’s bylaw enforcement department during the most-recent Canada Day holiday period, which ran from June 26 through July 2. By comparison, 63 public complaints were received during 2025 Canada Day celebrations and 221 inspections of vendors at that time led to two charges for non-permitted sale of fireworks.

items.title: $35,000 in Stolen Merchandise Recovered as Mississauga Man Faces Dozens of Theft Charges
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, Peel police say a 49-year-old Mississauga man has been charged with more than three dozen offences after a two-month investigation into a suspected prolific retail thief. The outlet reports the investigation, dubbed Project Bishop, began in April after officers identified a suspect believed to be behind numerous thefts of clothing and accessories from major retailers. Mississauga.com reports police linked the man to at least 38 theft-related incidents across Peel, Halton, Durham, York and Niagara regions, with the value of stolen merchandise in each incident ranging from about $50 to more than $4,000. According to the outlet, the man was arrested on June 19 and charged with 24 counts of theft under $5,000 and 14 counts of possession of property obtained by crime. Mississauga.com reports that following the arrest, search warrants executed at homes in Mississauga and Welland turned up more than $35,000 worth of stolen merchandise, including clothing, cosmetics and personal accessories.

items.title: Orange-level severe thunderstorm watch issued for Mississauga
items.summary: Residents are urged to prepare for potentially dangerous weather this afternoon and evening as Environment and Climate Change Canada issues an Orange-level Severe Thunderstorm Watch for Mississauga. Emergency and public safety | September 2, 2026 Environment and Climate Change Canada is warning that conditions are favourable for the development of severe thunderstorms capable of producing damaging winds, large hail, torrential rainfall and possible tornadoes. The weather system is expected to develop this afternoon and continue into the evening bringing a risk of damaging wind gusts, hail, and heavy rain. Forecast confidence is high, and residents are encouraged to stay informed and be prepared to take shelter if conditions deteriorate. In addition to the severe thunderstorm watch, the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority (TRCA) has issued a flood watch notice, while Credit Valley Conservation (CVC) has issued a flood outlook notice. Heavy rainfall may cause water levels to rise quickly in rivers, streams, creeks and stormwater systems. Residents are encouraged to stay away from shorelines, waterways and other areas where conditions may become dangerous. Periods of heavier rain may lead to higher water levels across the city. The wooden fence next to the construction site on Woodlawn Avenue has collapsed, exposing the adjacent property. A soil collapse at the site of a Port Credit housing development has left neighbouring homeowners wondering who is responsible for oversight after their property was damaged. Carl and Mari-Anne McCleary, who live adjacent to the Woodlawn Avenue construction site in Mississauga’s Credit Grove neighbourhood, say a deep excavation has remained open along their property line for nearly a year. The couple said soil began washing into the pit in May. The erosion destroyed their garden and glass greenhouse before their wooden fence collapsed into the pit, leaving an open drop-off along their lot line they say is unsafe for their pets. The Woodlawn Avenue site seen here, with water pooling and a construction vehicle on site, in late May 2026.

items.title: Bombardier to acquire MHI Canada Aerospace assets in Mississauga
items.summary: Bombardier and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI) have entered into an agreement under which Bombardier will acquire the assets of MHI Canada Aerospace (MHICA) in Mississauga, Ontario. The transaction is expected to close later this year, subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions. Bombardier will add MHICA’s aerostructure manufacturing capabilities and its roughly 750 employees to support its aircraft programmes. MHICA traces its origins to 1996, when MHI initiated a consortium of independent contractors operating within Bombardier’s manufacturing facility to undertake final completion activities and address outstanding work on products originating from Japan. MHICA was officially incorporated in Ontario in 2006. In 2007, it acquired a 90,000 square foot facility to begin assembly of Global wings, centre fuselage integration and systems installation for products sourced from MHI Japan, and the following year took on Challenger series wing assembly and systems installation. In 2012, the company relocated from its Meadowvale facility to a roughly 270,000 square foot site in Mississauga, which also enabled the relocation of Global 5500/6500 wing major assembly to Canada, and in 2013 it added a 70,000 square foot facility to house its Supply Chain and Logistics Centre. “This agreement represents a key step in Bombardier’s long-term growth strategy, strengthening critical capabilities, enhancing operational resilience and supporting the company’s flexibility to meet growing customer demand,” said David Murray, executive vice president, Manufacturing, Supply Chain Execution and Bombardier Operational Excellence System, Bombardier. ” MHI will support an orderly transition and provide transitional support for an interim period after closing to maintain continuity for MHICA’s operations and employees.
